title: Causal Fisher-Information Inequalities: Classical Causal Model Falsification and Metrological Advantage
summary: Fisher-information inequalities have recently been used as operational witnesses of nonclassical metrological behavior, but their physical meaning is often tied to a particular narrative, such as, segmented dynamics or discrete trajectories. We show that a broader interpretation is available and, in fact, more natural: once an experiment is assumed to admit a classical causal model specified by a directed acyclic graph, conditional independences, and modular parameter dependence, the corresponding Fisher informations are forced to obey causal Fisher-information inequalities (CFIIs).
